Definition: Creating content, like terrain, by following rules instead of making each part by hand.
Impossible to predict. A truly random result, like a fair dice roll, can't be known before it happens.
A number that looks random but is made by a formula. Start the formula the same way and it gives the same numbers again.
A starting number for a pseudo-random formula or a generator. The same seed and settings always give the same result.
Always giving the same output for the same input. A generator with a seed is deterministic, even though its result looks random.
A formula that turns a position into a value that changes smoothly from place to place, used to make natural-looking shapes.
A kind of smooth noise invented by Ken Perlin. Quorum Studio builds all of its terrain presets from it.
One layer of noise. Each octave is finer and smaller than the one before it, and adding several together makes ground with both big shapes and small detail.
Several octaves of noise added together, which makes rolling, natural-looking ground.
Noise folded so it makes sharp crests, used for mountain ridges.
Noise turned the other way from ridged noise, so it cuts sharp valleys into high ground, used for canyons.
Turning smooth heights into flat steps with steep sides between them, used for plateaus.
A saved set of generator settings, such as Rolling hills or Mountains.
A simulation of rain wearing ground down, which makes generated terrain look more natural.
A whole shape, such as a hill or a crater, pressed into the terrain at the brush.
